title: Which Net Folds into a Cube?
summary: Pick a base square and fold the rest around it in your mind.

steps.title: The puzzle
sentences: You cut it along some edges and open it flat.
Which flat shapes of 6 squares can fold back into a cube?

steps.title: How to think about it
sentences: Imagine folding. Squares that would overlap cannot be in the same place.
points: Imagine folding. Squares that would overlap cannot be in the same place.

steps.title: The method: Fold in the mind
sentences: A row of 4 squares with one square above and one below, anywhere along the row, folds into a cube.
A row of 5 squares in a line cannot, because the first and the fifth would meet in the same place after wrapping around.
Four in a row is a handy starter.
points: A row of 4 squares with one square above and one below, anywhere along the row, folds into a cube.

steps.title: The answer
sentences: There are 11 different nets that fold into a cube.
Check by imagining that one square is the bottom and walking around it.
If any two squares land in the same face, it fails.
points: There are 11 different nets that fold into a cube.

facts: There are exactly 11 distinct nets of a cube.

quiz.q: How many faces does a cube have?
